tasks.title: Public-facing docs: vision, architecture, ADR log, CONTRIBUTING
tasks.description: Write the public renditions that a visitor to the repo needs: docs/vision.md, docs/architecture.md, the first ADRs recording decisions already made (single-HTML source, no ZIP container, no arbitrary script in the native profile, toolchain), and a brief CONTRIBUTING.md. These are condensed public documents derived from the plan/docs/ design pack, not copies of it. Also define the conformance programme that TRADEMARKS.md defers, so that claims of FRWD compatibility have a published, testable standard behind them, and decide whether to promote the normative format spec into spec/FRWD-0.1.md at that point.

tasks.title: CV reference document
tasks.description: The last of the designed corpus, deliberately lowest priority: the business report already demonstrates dense designed two-column content, so this is confirmation rather than evidence. Dense typographic layout and print fidelity in a single page.

tasks.title: Editor shell hardening and end-to-end browser tests
tasks.description: Two bugs manual use found, plus the E2E coverage that would have found them. First: a non-conforming or non-native document is displayed and diagnosed but must not be mutable at all - no region mounting, no text editing, no formatting, no insert/move/theme operations, no saving over as though it were native FRWD. Opening a .frwd.html publication currently refuses operations but still lets text regions mount, which contradicts the load pipeline written down in t-023. Enforced at the session boundary rather than only in the shell, so the rule holds wherever it is called from, and the native file picker stops offering generic .html. Second: toolbar bold, italic and link do nothing because the global outside-surface mousedown handler commits the region before the click handler runs; the toolbar must preserve the active region, its selection and enough focus to apply a mark, without letting chrome leak into canonical state. Then a Playwright project that launches the editor server and drives the real UI: the native happy path through formatting, insert, move, theme token, undo, redo and save with the saved output re-parsed and re-validated; the unsafe path proving read-only really is read-only and the source is untouched; and a regression that uses the actual toolbar buttons rather than region-model methods. Scope stays narrow - no drag and drop, no property panels, no importer, no AI panel.

tasks.title: Contextual block editing and direct manipulation
tasks.description: Make the document feel structurally editable rather than adding more toolbar commands, and establish the selection and container model the later style/layout inspector will depend on. A real editor selection model distinguishing the selected FRWD object, the active text region, the object parent and its position among siblings - all editor state, never written into the canonical tree. Contextual insertion that reasons from the actual semantic parent: a sibling paragraph in ordinary flow, another li inside a list, content staying inside the card or section it belongs to, and a refusal with an explanation where the context is genuinely ambiguous, with no fixture class names hard-coded and new ids minted through one shared path rather than inferred from the shape of existing ones. This is an editor tool compiling to existing structural operations, not a new normative FRWD operation. Direct reordering by dragging a handle, deliberately narrow: identified sibling blocks within one parent, committed through move_node, with cross-container drags refused rather than guessed - drag changes semantic order in flow, it does not turn a flowing document into a canvas. A minimal breadcrumb so nested selection is understandable. Shell end-to-end coverage through the real UI for contextual insertion in flow and list contexts, drag reorder with the id travelling and undo/redo, nested selection, and a save that re-parses conforming and inside the safety profile. Not in scope: cross-parent dragging, pixel positioning, spacing or property panels, CSS editing, page/flow modes, AI panel, multi-block text selection.

tasks.title: Selected-object style and layout inspector
tasks.description: Make the visual document directly adjustable without turning FRWD into a canvas or letting the editor rewrite arbitrary stylesheet text. Adds two core operations, set_style_property and remove_style_property, editing exactly one identified element inline declaration block through a real CSS declaration model rather than string surgery: unrelated declarations preserved, staged and atomic and prepared-transaction compatible, unsafe values refused rather than sanitized, styleLocked rejects and contentLocked permits, and the change record names target, property and value. They are core because their meaning is deterministic - two implementations must agree what setting property X to value Y on element Z means - while make_card_prettier and make_three_columns stay editor tools. Three styling levels stay distinct: set_theme_token for document-wide tokens, document-defined classes through the existing attribute operation with no FRWD enum of variant names, and the new operation for deliberate local overrides. Shared CSS selector rules are explicitly out of scope, because changing one affects many objects and raises a different scope question. Adds a properties sidebar for the current selection covering spacing, sizing and alignment, contextual grid columns and gap, a small appearance set, and the element class list, distinguishing an inherited or rule-derived value from a local override and offering a way to clear one. getComputedStyle is read-only evidence about what rendered; the canonical state stays the FRWD DOM and its CSS, and selecting an object with no edit stays a no-op. No fixture class names anywhere. Not in scope: shared rule editing, stylesheet source editing, free positioning, breakpoint editor, page size, page/flow modes, AI panel, importer, collaboration.

tasks.title: View modes and a pagination architecture spike
tasks.description: Not a pagination engine. Make the editor distinguish three things that have been blurring together: the document real screen CSS, an editor paper visualisation, and actual print output. Spike what a browser can honestly tell a page about print - @page rules, break positions, page count, page boxes - and answer whether native primitives can support a trustworthy embedded print preview or whether FRWD eventually needs a paged-media layer, recording the answer as an ADR if it has architectural consequences. Explicitly do not fake page boundaries by dividing scrollHeight by A4 height. Then implement only the safe controls: an editor viewport switcher (fit, mobile, tablet, desktop) that changes the projection and not the document, and a paper frame that is editor chrome, with the document own fixed geometry preserved faithfully where a document defines it - a CV that declares .sheet { width: 210mm } is document CSS, not evidence that FRWD is page-based. Surface any @page declaration as information; the paper choice is an editor preference and @page is document state, and the two must not leak into each other. If trustworthy embedded preview is unavailable, prefer the real browser print engine over a fake in-editor paginator. Regression coverage for both a flowing fixture and a deliberately fixed-geometry one, proving view switching leaves the canonical source byte-identical with no revision or undo entry. Out of scope: a pagination engine or dependency, automatic fitting to N pages, editing @page through the UI, breakpoint editor, shared CSS-rule editor, importer, AI panel.

tasks.title: Give the projection its own viewport so responsive preview is real
tasks.description: Found while building the view switcher in t-028. Narrowing the projection container reflows anything container-relative - grids, flex, percentage widths, text measure - but does not trigger the document @media queries, because those evaluate against the browser window and no amount of resizing a div changes that. The mobile and tablet views therefore preview width, not responsiveness, and are labelled that way rather than pretending otherwise, with a test pinning the limitation so it cannot be mistaken for working. Making it real means hosting the projection in an iframe so it owns a viewport. That is a genuine change rather than a tweak: the region editor, the drag handle, the breadcrumb and every listener currently assume a single document, and ProseMirror would be mounting into another one. Worth doing - author once and inspect the same document across breakpoints is one of the format most useful claims - but worth doing deliberately.
